title: sdk: consolidate auth, retry logic and streaming parity across Python/TS/Go
author: Anika Shah
description:
Motivation: multiple SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) had diverging behaviors around authentication refresh, transient retry semantics, and the streaming API surface. This caused user confusion and intermittent production regressions when teams switched SDKs or upgraded individual client libs.

This PR unifies three areas: auth token refresh middleware, retry/backoff semantics for 429/5xxs, and streaming helper ergonomics (client- and server-facing helpers). The goal is parity for common primitives and ergonomics improvements without changing server-side contracts.

Summary of changes: 
- Introduced a shared auth adapter behavior (same refresh triggers and single-flight refresh) implemented in each SDK idiomatically.
- Standardized retry policy: idempotency map + jittered exponential backoff with capped attempts and configurable per-client override. 429s use a longer initial backoff and honor Retry-After when present.
- Streaming: added unified client helpers (Python async iterator, TS async generator, Go channel helper) that surface an identical framing behavior and consistent early-close semantics.
- Ergonomics: better default timeouts, simpler initialization interface (Auth + Retry optional struct/object), and improved error classes/messages for transient vs terminal errors.
- Docs and CHANGELOG entries for each SDK and small example apps demonstrating streaming with reconnect versus fail-fast semantics.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement auth single-flight refresh in Python, TS, Go
- [x] Align retry/backoff config across SDKs
- [x] Add streaming helper primitives + examples
- [x] Add unit and e2e tests (local harness + CI)
- [x] Update SDK docs and migration notes

Migration notes: default retry and auth behavior is backward-compatible for existing users. Users who rely on very aggressive retry policies should audit the new defaults; an escape hatch exists via client config. Streaming helper API additions are additive; previous low-level streaming primitives remain available.

References: Linear ENG-4890 (unify SDK semantics), ENG-4912 (streaming reliability improvements).
